01 · What are hackathons?

What is a hackathon?

A short event where teams build a project around a problem or theme.

Projects can include
WebsitesAppsAI / ML toolsGamesHardwareData projects
How it ends

A demo to judges

The good news

You do not need to be an advanced programmer

Typical structure

How a hackathon flows

Photo: Randymcking · CC BY-SA 3.0
01Theme / challenge announced
02Form a team
03Choose a problem
04Plan an MVP
05Build the project
06Test the demo
07Present to judges
The word to remember
MVP
What it stands for

Minimum viable product

The smallest version of the project that proves the main idea works.

The rule

A polished working feature is better than many unfinished features

02 · How to prepare

Before the hackathon

Everyone should still understand the overall project.

Make sure you have:
GitHub account
Git installed
VS Code or another IDE
Laptop + charger
Development environment ready
Accounts / API keys for tools you may use
Team roles
Frontend
Backend
AI / ML
UI / UX
Presentation / demo
02 · Build it well

A strong project

Simple formula
Problem Solution Demo Impact
Focus on
01Specific problem
02Clear target user
03One strong core feature
04Working demo
05Clean UI
06Meaningful use of AI
07Clear real-world impact
A · Example

Education

  • AI study assistant
  • Accessibility tool
  • Personalized learning system
B · Example

Environment

  • Energy usage optimizer
  • Waste classification system
  • Environmental data dashboard
C · Example

Civic / Community

  • Public service assistant
  • Community issue reporting system
  • Resource matching platform
D · Example

AI / Automation

  • Voice assistant
  • Agentic workflow tool
  • Document or data automation system
Avoid building:Generic chatbotBasic to-do appHuge project, too many features

Solve one real problem well.

04 · How to win

Strong projects usually have

01Important problem
02Original solution
03Working prototype
04Technical depth
05Clean design
06Clear impact
07Strong presentation
Presentation structure
01What is the problem?
02Why does it matter?
03What did we build?
04Demo
05How does it work?
06What impact could it have?

Practice the demo before presenting.
